codings.one_line: Fast-food hiring chatbots at McDonald's, Wendy's, and Hardee's failed to properly schedule or relay interview info to applicants.
codings.rationale: Applicants used the bots exactly as intended for ordinary job applications (C); the result was frustration and missed communication with no documented legal/financial consequence (reputational).

codings.one_line: A user got Bing Chat's image-analysis feature to solve CAPTCHAs despite the feature being safeguarded against that use.
codings.rationale: The user deliberately probed whether an intended safety restriction (refusing to solve CAPTCHAs) could be bypassed via image upload, a technical exploit of a safeguard (A); Microsoft disabled the feature with no documented legal/financial fallout (reputational).

codings.one_line: Australian grant peer reviewers allegedly fed confidential applications into ChatGPT to produce assessment reports.
codings.rationale: The documented harm is a confidentiality breach from sharing applicants' data with a third-party AI tool, not a false or harmful conversational output relied upon within an interaction; closer to the excluded data-handling category.

codings.one_line: Third parties built unfiltered NSFW/violent roleplay chatbots (e.g. 'Allie') on Meta's open-source LLaMA model.
codings.rationale: This describes third parties repurposing an open-weight base model to build unofficial chatbots, without a documented specific triggering interaction or victim, similar to the excluded synthetic-content-by-third-parties category.

codings.one_line: Kremlin-linked firms allegedly used generative AI to mass-produce disinformation articles for Latin American media.
codings.rationale: This is a state-run propaganda content-generation campaign amplified via bots, matching the excluded synthetic-media-generation-by-third-parties category rather than a deployed AI's direct harmful interaction with an end user.

codings.one_line: A ChatGPT-generated book with a duplicate title and fake author appeared on Amazon ahead of a real author's book release.
codings.rationale: A publisher mass-produced synthetic text to imitate and compete with a real work, matching the excluded synthetic-content-generation-by-third-parties category rather than a harmful conversational interaction.

codings.one_line: Google's search AI (including its generative SGE feature) told users no African country starts with 'K,' among other geography errors.
codings.rationale: Users asked plain factual questions ('what is an African country beginning with K'), ordinary good-faith traffic (C); the misinformation embarrassed Google with no documented legal/financial consequence (reputational).

codings.one_line: Academics used Google Bard to generate case studies for a parliamentary inquiry, producing false misconduct allegations against KPMG and Deloitte.
codings.rationale: Using Bard for ordinary academic research is good-faith use consistent with the tool's purpose (C); the firms suffered reputational harm and received an apology, but parliamentary privilege barred any lawsuit, so harm is reputational.

codings.one_line: A Colorado attorney cited ChatGPT-hallucinated case law in a court motion, which was denied; he was reported to a disciplinary body and fired.
codings.rationale: Ordinary legal research use of ChatGPT is good-faith, unremarkable traffic (C); the denied motion, disciplinary referral, and firing are documented professional/legal consequences (enforceable).

codings.one_line: A user tricked a Chevrolet dealer's ChatGPT-powered chatbot into 'agreeing' to sell a Tahoe for $1.
codings.rationale: The user explicitly instructed the bot to agree with anything to manufacture a viral screenshot, deliberate goading with no technical exploit (B); the dealer deactivated the bot with no documented financial loss since the offer wasn't honored (reputational).
